## Tours featuring Spinoglio Winery: 4 days of Uruguayan wine and history

[Spinoglio Winery](/uruguay/place/spinoglio-winery/) is north of Montevideo. This historic estate combines vineyards, an old stone cellar and oak barrels. A visit introduces travelers to winemaking and an opportunity to taste local wines where they are produced.

We include the winery on our [4-day “Uruguay: Wine and Old Believer Traditions” tour](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/). The route combines gastronomy, the history of settlers from Russia, the industrial heritage of Fray Bentos and the architecture of Colonia del Sacramento. **The visit to Bodega Spinoglio is one of the central days, but it is not the only purpose of the journey.**

## What's included at Bodega Spinoglio

On day 2, after breakfast, travelers depart Montevideo. The drive to the estate takes approximately 30 minutes. During the tour, they discover the vineyards, production facilities and century-old cellar. Stone walls and large oak barrels illustrate the development of winemaking over generations.

**A tasting of four wines is included**, accompanied by cheeses, bread and appetizers prepared by the chef. Guests then return to Montevideo for the night. The current itinerary does not proceed directly from the winery to the next town; the westward journey continues the following morning.

The winery itself offers several excursion and dining options, as confirmed by its official website. They are not identical to the services included by Ada Tours. Extra lunches, expanded tastings or alternative tours through several bodegas are not automatically included simply because the estate offers them.

## What else will travelers see?

On day 1, guests explore [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/): its civic squares, coastal districts, gastronomy and evening music scene. After the winery day, the route heads west to San Javier, a settlement linked to Russian migrants of the early 20th century. The program includes meeting local residents and discovering the family histories of the community.

The next stop is Fray Bentos. The program includes the Anglo Museum, dedicated to the history of the meat-processing industry. The Fray Bentos Industrial Landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Uruguay's wine story is thus complemented by a very different history of production and international commerce.

On the final day, the itinerary explores historic Colonia del Sacramento, with architecture dating to the Portuguese and Spanish eras. After sightseeing, travelers arrive at the dock for a ferry to Buenos Aires. Museum entrance tickets in Colonia are **not included** in the price, which matters when planning independent visits.

| Day | Main focus |
|---|---|
| 1 | Montevideo, urban culture and gastronomy |
| 2 | Spinoglio: vineyards, cellar and four wines |
| 3 | San Javier and the history of Russian settlers |
| 4 | Fray Bentos, Colonia del Sacramento and ferry |

## Who will enjoy the Spinoglio itinerary?

This journey is chosen for its combination of wine and national history. Unlike a brief winery visit, it provides wider context, from Montevideo and wine production to historic settlements and industrial monuments.

If your sole purpose is tasting wines from many vintages, visiting several wineries and enjoying lengthy gastronomic lunches, do not treat the 4-day program as an already arranged multi-day wine festival. It confirms one visit to Bodega Spinoglio with a four-wine tasting.

Our selection currently contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Accommodation, transport, excursions and exclusions are set out in the [complete 4-day itinerary](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/). For other culinary destinations, explore [Food and Wine](/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Spinoglio

### How many wines are tasted during the visit?

The Ada Tours itinerary specifies a tasting of four wines with cheeses, bread and chef-prepared appetizers. Other tasting packages offered by the winery are separate products.

### Must you travel to the winery on your own?

No. On the described 4-day trip, excursions and transfers along the route are included. Day 2 begins with departure from Montevideo, followed by a return to the capital.

### Is an overnight stay at the winery included?

No. Guests return to Montevideo after the excursion. The journey continues toward San Javier the following morning.

### Does the tour finish in Montevideo?

No. After Colonia del Sacramento, the itinerary includes a ferry to Buenos Aires, where the included services end. Travel onward to another city is not part of the program unless separately specified.

## Excursions to Punta Ballena: the headland, Casapueblo and travel from Montevideo

[Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/) lies on Uruguay's coast near [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/). Visitors come for views from the rocky headland and Casapueblo, the extraordinary white house of artist Carlos Páez Vilaró. A stop at the headland is easy to combine with nearby coastal resorts, but a brief viewpoint stop and a detailed museum visit require different amounts of time.

We offer Punta Ballena as part of an [excursion from Montevideo via Piriápolis and Punta del Este](/uruguay/montevideo/punta-del-este-piriapolis-from-montevideo/). It lasts 8 hours. This itinerary covers several coastal destinations, so the length of the Casapueblo stop should be agreed before departure.

## What's included at Punta Ballena?

After [Piriápolis](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/), our program continues to Punta Ballena. The itinerary includes **Casapueblo**, associated with the life and work of Carlos Páez Vilaró. It then proceeds to Punta del Este before returning to Montevideo.

An English-speaking guide and transfers are confirmed for the trip. This is convenient for travelers wishing to explore coastal towns without arranging each transfer independently. However, the itinerary **does not specify whether a separate museum admission ticket to Casapueblo is included**. Its price should not be assumed to be covered simply because the building is named.

The [Casapueblo museum and workshop](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/) itself features the artist's work, terraces and organic architecture. According to the museum, its galleries contain paintings, ceramics and sculpture. If art is your priority, allow time to explore the interior collection rather than simply photographing the white facade.

## Choosing the time of your Casapueblo visit

| Option | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Daytime stop | Architecture and coastal views |
| Museum visit | Works by Páez Vilaró and terraces |
| Evening visit | Possibility of watching the sunset |

A daytime visit is convenient when Punta Ballena is one of several stops. In clear weather, views open along the coastline; in strong winds, use safe paths and viewpoints. The museum's interior exhibition is best explored without rushing.

Casapueblo's well-known sunset tradition is another reason to come in the evening. However, **participation in the sunset ceremony is not confirmed on our 8-hour excursion from Montevideo**. Sunset times vary through the year, and the route covers several places. An evening visit would require a different order of stops and onward transport from the museum, subject to arrangements.

Check current opening hours and ticket sales conditions for the specific date. These should not be confused with the excursion's timetable.

## How Punta Ballena differs from Piriápolis and Punta del Este

The three stops have different strengths. [Piriápolis](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/) offers a historic resort, waterfront promenade and views from San Antonio Hill. [Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/) features artistic architecture on a rocky coast. [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) introduces the peninsula, beaches and resort life.

Their combination makes sense for a first coastal excursion from [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). But if you want a tour exclusively about art history or an extended sunset experience, a brief visit to all three places may feel too packed. Discuss a tailored itinerary focusing on one destination rather than assuming unconfirmed services will be available.

## What to check before choosing the excursion

First decide your priority: views from the headland, Casapueblo's interiors or evening light over the coast. Then confirm these points against the exact program:

- **Route and departure.** Our excursion starts in Montevideo and also visits Piriápolis and Punta del Este.
- **Museum admission.** Confirm whether the ticket is included and how much time is allocated to the exhibition.
- **Return journey.** For a sunset visit, clarify evening transport and driving time separately.

The [“Punta del Este and Piriápolis from Montevideo” excursion](/uruguay/montevideo/punta-del-este-piriapolis-from-montevideo/) includes 8 hours, transfers and an English-speaking guide. Lunch is paid for separately. A winery stop on the return journey may be added, with the tasting paid separately. These terms belong to that particular product and should not automatically be applied to a custom excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about Punta Ballena excursions

### Can you visit Punta Ballena from Montevideo in a day?

Yes. Our 8-hour excursion includes Punta Ballena between Piriápolis and Punta del Este.

### Is admission to Casapueblo included?

The itinerary does not confirm a museum ticket. Before booking, ask about entry to the galleries, the admission price and the length of the stop.

### Will we attend Casapueblo's sunset ceremony?

Only if the itinerary is specifically arranged for an evening visit. Mentioning Casapueblo in the description does not itself guarantee attendance.

### Can you continue from Punta Ballena to Punta del Este?

Yes. That is the route on our current [coastal excursion](/uruguay/montevideo/punta-del-este-piriapolis-from-montevideo/). If a longer stay in Punta del Este is the priority, explore the [resort itself](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) before choosing a format.

### Which excursions appear on this page?

This page lists excursions that include Punta Ballena. The [Punta Ballena destination page](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/) separately describes the headland and Casapueblo.

## Best of Uruguay in 6 days: Montevideo, Punta del Este and two wineries

This itinerary lasts **6 days and 5 nights**. The first 3 nights are in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), followed by 2 nights in [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/). The program includes private transfers and city tours, visits to Bouza and Garzón wineries with gastronomic lunches, and sunset at Casapueblo.

Wine culture is a central feature of this itinerary. The wineries occupy two separate days, each including a lunch paired with wine. This sets the program apart from a route devoted only to cities and beaches.

## Three nights in Montevideo

On day 1, guests are met at the airport or port and transferred to Hyatt Centric Montevideo. The next day begins with a private tour of [Uruguay's capital](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) in English.

Stops include Independence Square, the Citadel Gate, Solís Theatre, Palacio Salvo, Avenida 18 de Julio, the Legislative Palace, the agricultural market, Parque Batlle y Ordóñez and Estadio Centenario. The final part of the city tour follows the coastal Rambla.

The excursion introduces historic architecture, everyday city life and the modern Atlantic waterfront. To enjoy a comfortable pace, discuss the stops and walking time beforehand; this is easier with a private tour than on a large-group sightseeing bus.

## Bouza Winery: a three-course wine-pairing lunch

On day 3, the itinerary visits [Bouza Winery](/uruguay/place/bouza-winery/), including an introduction to the estate and vineyards and a **3-course lunch**, each course accompanied by a selected wine.

This gastronomic stop is an experience in its own right: guests can compare food-and-wine pairings and discover how the estate's characteristics influence production. After lunch, they return to Montevideo.

If anyone in the group prefers a non-alcoholic option, discuss a possible alternative to wine pairings in advance. A particular alternative menu is not guaranteed.

## Punta del Este and sunset at Casapueblo

Day 4 starts with a private transfer to [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) and check-in at The Grand Punta del Este. After arrival, a private tour explores the resort: its peninsula, harbor, old lighthouse, market, coastal neighborhoods and La Mano sculpture.

The final stop is [Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/) and the famous Casapueblo, the museum and architectural complex of artist Carlos Páez Vilaró. **Admission to Casapueblo and sunset with a glass of champagne are included in the package.** This is an organized visit with a transfer, not merely a suggestion to reach the viewpoint independently.

## Garzón: the Reserva experience and four courses

Day 5 is dedicated to [Garzón Winery](/uruguay/place/garzon-winery/). The confirmed itinerary includes an estate tour, tastings and a **seasonal 4-course lunch** paired with wines. Bodega Garzón's official website lists the Reserva format among its distinct wine experiences.

Bouza and Garzón allow guests to compare two different estates through separate tastings. Consider that much of these two days is devoted to gastronomy rather than additional museums or beach outings. After Garzón, travelers return to their Punta del Este hotel.

On day 6, a private transfer takes guests to Montevideo airport or port.

## Hotels and price

We offer two five-star accommodation options on this itinerary:

| Location | Nights and room |
|---|---|
| Montevideo | 3, Hyatt Centric, River View |
| Punta del Este | 2, The Grand, Ocean View Junior |

Prices start **from $2418**. The package includes 5 nights with breakfast, all specified private transfers, city tours in English, both winery tastings and lunches, admission to Casapueblo and sunset with champagne. Additional excursions cost extra.

Under the tour terms, hotels may be replaced if necessary by others of the same category. When comparing offers, check not only the overall price but also the exact room category and the included excursions and lunches.

## Who will enjoy this itinerary?

It suits travelers who want comfortable accommodation combined with private city excursions and wine-focused gastronomy. It can also work as one part of a larger South American trip: the principal transfers within Uruguay are by road, and guests do not change hotels every day.

If beach relaxation is your main goal, compare programs by their free days. Here the main experiences are already scheduled: two cities, two wineries and Casapueblo. Other options are available in the [Uruguay tour catalog](/uruguay/tour/) and [food and wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/uruguay/).

## Frequently asked questions about the five-star Uruguay tour

### How many nights are spent in Punta del Este?

Two. The first three nights are in Montevideo.

### How many wineries are included?

Two: Bouza with a 3-course lunch and Garzón with a 4-course lunch.

### Are the excursions conducted in Russian?

The private tours are **in English**. Another language must be arranged separately.

### Is Casapueblo included?

Yes. Admission and an organized sunset visit are part of the program.

## Tours to Uruguay: choosing the right itinerary

The Ada Tours catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Uruguay among the main countries visited. But a country appearing in the itinerary does not necessarily mean a substantial journey through it. Some programs spend every day in Uruguay; others make only a stop between major stages in Argentina, Brazil, Chile or Paraguay.

## Traveling only in Uruguay: 4 or 6 days

### Four-day tour: wine and the history of Russian settlers

[“Wine and Old Believer Traditions”](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/) is a journey through several cultural regions. Day 1 takes place in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Day 2 features the capital and [Spinoglio Winery](/uruguay/place/spinoglio-winery/), including wine production and a tasting. Day 3 leads to [San Javier](/uruguay/place/san-javier/) and [Fray Bentos](/uruguay/place/fray-bentos/), while day 4 connects the Anglo Museum and [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/).

The appeal lies in the combination of winemaking, life in a Russian-settler community and historical landmarks. San Javier is associated with a settlement of migrants from Russia who arrived in 1913. Yet the tour's name does not establish that all residents or every founder belonged to the Old Believer religious tradition. This stop is better understood as an introduction to Russian historical and cultural heritage in Uruguay.

Fray Bentos preserves an industrial complex connected to the global history of meat production and exports. Its industrial landscape was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List in 2015. The historic quarter of Colonia, recognized by UNESCO in 1995, reveals a blend of Portuguese and Spanish urban traditions.

Four days offer a substantial cultural experience for travelers interested in history and wine. However, the itinerary does not include a multi-day beach holiday on the Atlantic coast. If the ocean is your priority, choose another route.

### Six-day tour: capital, wineries and ocean

The [“Best of Uruguay: Five-Star Tour”](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/) lasts 6 days. It combines [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), two winery visits and [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/). The opening days focus on the capital and gastronomy, followed by time on the resort coast.

This program suits travelers who want to alternate city walks, tastings and time by the Atlantic. Compared with the 4-day journey, it pays less attention to the Russian colony and Fray Bentos, but includes several days around Punta del Este.

Southern Uruguay's wine routes are associated with [Canelones](/uruguay/place/canelones/) and the tradition of growing Tannat grapes. The actual estates, tasting format and meals are specified on the selected tour page. Additional choices appear among [Uruguay food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/uruguay/).

The word “five-star” in a title does not replace checking the category of each hotel. Do not assume a 5-star hotel every night, a personal driver or any other services unless the program specifies them.

**Which should you choose: 4 or 6 days?** The 4-day route places more emphasis on western Uruguay's history and a particular winery; the 6-day route combines the capital, wine and the resort coast.

## Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay in 13 days: a real seaside stay

The [13-day tour through three countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) begins in Rio de Janeiro, continues to Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires, and only then reaches Uruguay. Travelers cross the Río de la Plata from Argentina, visiting [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/), [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/).

Day 7 includes the crossing and journey via Colonia to Montevideo, day 8 focuses on the capital, and day 9 is the road journey to Punta del Este. Several days of coastal relaxation follow; the route includes four nights in Punta del Este. Thus Uruguay is more than a symbolic stamp for visiting another country.

It is a good option for combining tropical Brazil, Argentina's capital and Uruguay's ocean coast in one holiday. It is not, however, an in-depth exploration of Uruguay: [San Javier](/uruguay/place/san-javier/) and [Fray Bentos](/uruguay/place/fray-bentos/) are not included in these 13 days.

Dates matter if the purpose is a beach holiday. Southern Hemisphere summer brings a livelier resort season and more visitors to Punta del Este. Weather and season have a different significance for urban sightseeing, so decide on your main travel goal in advance.

## Sixteen days: Uruguay, Paraguay and Iguazu

The [16-day Uruguay and Paraguay journey](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) starts with five days in Uruguay. Guests first explore [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/), then visit [Canelones](/uruguay/place/canelones/) for a Tannat tasting, continue to [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) and return to the capital. Only then does the Paraguayan segment begin.

The next major section includes Asunción, the Chaco, rural settlements and natural areas of Paraguay. The journey concludes at Iguazu Falls, visiting the Brazilian and Argentine sides. This creates a clear transition from cities and coastline to the interior of the continent.

Choose this route if Paraguayan culture and nature interest you alongside the Uruguayan opening. The [13-day Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay option](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) offers a different experience: Rio and beach relaxation are more prominent there, while the 16-day itinerary centers on the less familiar route through the Chaco.

## When Uruguay occupies just one day

Two longer journeys include Uruguay but devote most of their days to other countries.

On the [17-day itinerary through Chile, Argentina, Uruguay and Brazil](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/), travelers visit Santiago, Patagonia, Buenos Aires, Iguazu, Rio de Janeiro and Búzios. Uruguay is represented by a one-day trip from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/).

The [26-day Argentina and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) has the same format: a day trip Buenos Aires–Montevideo–Buenos Aires, with the remainder mainly devoted to Iguazu, northwestern Argentina, Mendoza, Bariloche, El Calafate, El Chaltén and Ushuaia.

**Do not confuse the total length of a journey with time in Uruguay.** A 26-day tour does not necessarily offer a deeper introduction to the country than a standalone 4-day one. If you want to see [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/), [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) or wineries, check that these places are actually included.

## Comparing cultural, wine and beach itineraries

For **wine**, both standalone tours are suitable, especially the [4-day Spinoglio program](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/). The 16-day multi-country itinerary also includes [Canelones](/uruguay/place/canelones/) and a tasting. Travelers who want wineries to occupy a substantial share of their holiday can explore our [Uruguay wine-tour selection](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/uruguay/).

For **beach relaxation**, choose an itinerary with time in [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/). The 6-day route includes a resort segment, while the 13-day journey from Brazil and Argentina has several nights on the coast. A one-day Montevideo excursion is not a substitute for an ocean holiday.

For **history and culture**, the main choices are [Colonia](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/), [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and western Uruguay. [Fray Bentos](/uruguay/place/fray-bentos/) and [San Javier](/uruguay/place/san-javier/) feature specifically on the 4-day thematic itinerary. Compare other cultural routes in our [Uruguay culture and history catalog](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/uruguay/).

## Prices and trip arrangements

Prices are meaningful to compare only alongside included services: nights, transport types, international flights, meals, tastings and guiding may differ substantially. Two equally priced trips can offer very different experiences and amounts of time in the country.

A ferry crossing between Buenos Aires and Uruguay must fit the remainder of the itinerary. For journeys through several countries, travel documents and entry rules need to be checked for the traveler's nationality. These requirements cannot be inferred from a general tour title. When choosing dates, consider how much of the program involves city sightseeing and how much is devoted to the coast.

Confirmed inclusions are listed on individual pages in the [Uruguay tour catalog](/uruguay/tour/). The general catalog does not establish a universal hotel class, private transportation or a Russian-speaking guide for every offer.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are there tours only within Uruguay?

Yes. The [4-day culture and wine journey](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/) and the [6-day tour including Punta del Este](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/) both have main itineraries entirely within Uruguay.

### Which tour has more time by the ocean?

The [13-day three-country program](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) ends with several days in Punta del Este, including four nights at the resort. The [6-day version](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/) also visits Punta del Este, but the trip is shorter.

### Where can you learn about the history of Russian settlers?

The [4-day itinerary](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/) includes [San Javier](/uruguay/place/san-javier/) and [Fray Bentos](/uruguay/place/fray-bentos/), as part of a wine and history route.

### Can Uruguay and Paraguay be combined?

Yes. The [16-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) includes a substantial initial stage in Uruguay, continues through Paraguay and ends near Iguazu Falls.

### Does Uruguay feature in Patagonia tours?

Yes, but not necessarily for long. On the [26-day Argentina journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) occupies one day, with the remainder of the itinerary primarily in Argentina.

### Does “five-star” in a tour title guarantee a 5-star hotel every night?

No. The category and exact accommodation must be explicitly confirmed on the tour page. The title does not replace the list of published services.

## Uruguay in 4 days: wine, Russian traditions and colonial towns

The [“Uruguay: Wine and Old Believer Traditions” tour](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/) lasts **4 days and 3 nights**. It begins in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and then visits a winery, San Javier with its Russian cultural heritage, Fray Bentos and [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/).

The itinerary's appeal lies in combining a modern capital, winemaking traditions and migration history. It suits travelers wishing to discover Uruguay through particular places and people rather than limiting their visit to a single city overview.

## Montevideo: the waterfront and Old Town

On day 1, guests are met at Carrasco Airport, then begin a sightseeing tour of the capital. [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) stands beside the Río de la Plata, and its long Rambla promenade connects different urban neighborhoods.

Stops include Independence Square, historic buildings, markets, residential areas and the waterfront. [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/) and the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) show how modern city life remains connected to the colonial past.

Montevideo is a convenient starting point: travelers can sample Uruguayan cuisine, discover local products and see the first contrast between the port city and quieter parts of the country.

## Day 2: historic Bodega Spinoglio

The next day brings a visit to [Spinoglio Winery](/uruguay/place/spinoglio-winery/), about 30 minutes from the capital. The 19th-century winery combines vineyards, modern production and old underground spaces.

Its historic cellar, with substantial stone walls and oak barrels, is a particular highlight. The excursion includes the vineyards and production facilities, then **a tasting of 4 wines** with cheeses, bread and appetizers. This makes the day a distinct gastronomic experience rather than a brief photo stop.

Before the visit, it is useful to agree on the guiding language and tasting arrangements for guests who do not consume alcohol. Other wines and additional purchases should not automatically be regarded as included.

## San Javier: the history of Russian settlers

On day 3, the route leaves the capital and heads west to [San Javier](/uruguay/place/san-javier/). The settlement is associated with migrants from the Russian Empire who arrived in the early 20th century. During the visit, you will learn about the events of 1913 and family histories of the colony's founders.

Travelers encounter local traditions and may hear how generations of residents have preserved the memory of their ancestors. San Javier's history appeals both to those interested in migration and to people wishing to see an unfamiliar side of South America's cultural geography.

The tour title mentions “Old Believers,” while the visit itself chiefly concerns the Russian community and its descendants. **It would be inappropriate to assign the same religious identity to every present-day resident.** Meetings and personal accounts are arranged as part of the excursion.

## Fray Bentos and Colonia del Sacramento

Fray Bentos is the next stage. It preserves the Liebig and Anglo meat-processing industrial complex, recognized as UNESCO World Heritage in 2015. A visit to the Anglo Museum introduces another chapter of Uruguayan history: food exports to Europe, labor, industrial infrastructure and international trade.

The route concludes in [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/), with cobbled lanes and architecture bearing Portuguese and Spanish influences. After the industrial buildings of Fray Bentos, this historic town offers a very different view of the country.

**Admission tickets to museums in Colonia del Sacramento are listed among the exclusions.** Identify the museums you wish to visit and allow for the additional expense.

## What's included in the journey?

The price includes 3 nights of accommodation, breakfasts, scheduled excursions and transfers. Additional excursions, meals and drinks beyond the program, tips and Colonia museum admission tickets are paid separately.

## Frequently asked questions about the Uruguay itinerary

### How many wines are tasted?

At Spinoglio Winery, the program includes a tasting of 4 wines with appetizers.

### Will you meet descendants of Russian settlers?

San Javier is included as a historic community where meeting local residents is possible. The precise format and content of any meeting are arranged in the program.

### Why is Fray Bentos interesting to visitors?

The former Liebig/Anglo complex is part of a UNESCO World Heritage property. It tells the story of Uruguay's food industry within international commerce.

### Are all museum tickets included?

No. Admission to museums in Colonia del Sacramento is listed separately.
